# death penalty with a two-year reprieve

The death penalty execution system in China

![Image 1](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/ac345982b2b7d0a20cf4fe1543b361094b36adaf2cbc/ac345982b2b7d0a20cf4fe1543b361094b36adaf2cbc?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

What does death penalty with a two-year reprieve mean?(from:庭立方刑事律师平台)

01:37

![Image 2](https://gbaike-image.cdn.bcebos.com/b64543a98226cffc1e173fef8b5d5d90f603738dbc60/b64543a98226cffc1e173fef8b5d5d90f603738dbc60_url?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto/resize,m_lfit,w_400,limit_1)

Death penalty with a two-year reprieve, commonly referred to as a suspended death sentence, refers to a situation where a criminal who should be sentenced to death is, if immediate execution is not deemed absolutely necessary, sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve announced simultaneously, meaning the death sentence is suspended. The prerequisite for its application is that the offender must have committed "extremely serious crimes" warranting the Death Penalty. Cases of this type are also classified as death penalty cases.

1

On May 8, 1951, to curb extreme phenomena in the early years of the People's Republic of China, Chairman Mao Zedong drafted the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party on the Policy of Mostly Imposing Death Sentence with a Two-Year Reprieve on Counterrevolutionaries Who Have Committed Capital Crimes," formally introducing the term "suspended death sentence." On July 1, 1979, the "Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China" passed by the Second Session of the Fifth National People's Congress legally established the provision for the death penalty with a two-year reprieve. On March 14, 1997, the Second Session of the Eighth National People's Congress made substantial revisions to the Criminal Law, further standardizing the system of death penalty with a two-year reprieve. On February 25, 2011, the Nineteenth Session of the Eleventh National People's Congress passed a resolution for the eighth amendment to the Criminal Law, extending the "commutation period" and adding provisions for "restricted commutation." On August 29, 2015, the Standing Committee of the Twelfth National People's Congress made the ninth amendment to the Criminal Law, revising the content of the first paragraph of Article 50 concerning the death penalty with a two-year reprieve. On December 19, 2024, the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Standardization of the Delivery and Execution of Prisoners Sentenced to Imprisonment" clearly stipulated the time limit for transferring all legal documents when delivering a prisoner sentenced to a suspended death sentence for execution.

1

The death penalty with a two-year reprieve is an innovation of China, praised by Western countries as the "Eastern death penalty system." It holds unique historical, social, political, and legal significance. The substantive conditions for restricting commutation for offenders sentenced to suspended death are: restricted commutation for recidivists, restricted commutation for those sentenced to suspended death for the seven types of serious crimes, and restricted commutation for offenders sentenced to suspended death for organized violent crimes.

What does death penalty with suspension of execution mean?(from:普法刘同学)

Definition

Death penalty with a two-year reprieve, abbreviated as "suspended death sentence". It refers to a situation where, for a criminal who should be sentenced to death, if immediate execution is not deemed absolutely necessary, the death penalty may be imposed while simultaneously announcing a two-year reprieve, that is, a suspended execution of the death sentence. This penal system was proposed by Chairman Mao Zedong in the early years of the People's Republic of China. The suspended death sentence is not an independent category of punishment but rather a method of executing the death penalty.

1

Historical Evolution

Historical Background

In the early days of the founding of the People's Republic of China, counterrevolutionary activities were rampant across the country, seriously endangering the consolidation of state power, social stability, and economic recovery. From January to October 1950, China experienced 816 armed riots aimed at overthrowing the new government. On March 18 of the same year, Liu Shaoqi drafted the "Directive of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party on Suppressing Counterrevolutionary Activities" (commonly known as the "March 18 Directive"), which was the first special directive from the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party concerning the suppression of counterrevolutionaries after the founding of the People's Republic. In order to thoroughly complete the New Democratic Revolution, consolidate the nascent people's political power, and create a stable political situation and social environment, in October 1950, the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party launched the Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries nationwide, abbreviated as the "Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries."

7

Proposal and Establishment

*   Proposal of the "Suspended Death Sentence" 

On February 9, 1951, the "Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Punishing Counterrevolutionaries" (21 articles in total) were passed at the 71st Government Administration Council meeting and approved at the 11th meeting of the Central People's Government Committee on February 20 of the same year. This criminal law-specific regulation only stipulated matters related to the "Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries" and was similar to the subsequent special regulations for the "Three-Anti and Five-Anti Campaigns"; it did not contain any content regarding the "suspended death sentence." On April 30 of the same year, in order to curb some extreme phenomena that had emerged during the "Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries," Chairman Mao Zedong explicitly wrote in a written instruction: "We cannot kill too many people; killing too many will cause us to lose public sympathy and also waste labor power. In rural areas, the number of counterrevolutionaries executed generally should not exceed one-thousandth of the population. In special circumstances, this proportion can be exceeded, but approval from the Central Bureau is required and must be reported to the Central Committee for the record. In cities, the proportion generally should be less than one-thousandth." Mao Zedong also considered that merely proposing not to kill too many people and to control the number of executions was insufficient; specific policy limits must be established. Among the specific policy limits, Mao Zedong accurately pinpointed a key issue: how to separate a portion of people who should not be executed from among those who had committed capital offenses. To this end, in the aforementioned same instruction, he for the first time proposed the idea of having a "suspended death sentence" penalty. He wrote: "For those who have no blood debts or other major crimes that have aroused public indignation but are guilty of a capital offense, such as some spies or espionage agents, some counterrevolutionaries in educational or economic circles, etc., the death penalty may be imposed, but with a reprieve of one or two years, forcing them to labor and observe their subsequent performance. If they can reform through labor, then in the second step, their sentence may be commuted to life imprisonment, and in the third step, to a fixed-term imprisonment... In this way, the initiative is in our hands, and we can decide what to do later." Mao Zedong himself felt that proposing this idea was a matter of great importance and could not be decided immediately. Therefore, he suggested that this issue be discussed and decided at the public security conference scheduled for May 10. He also proposed: "Regarding this idea, please convey any opinions you may have through the public security personnel from your area who will attend the meeting in Beijing, or send a telegram." Before the national public security conference was held, Mao Zedong presented his idea of establishing the "suspended death sentence" penalty at a meeting of the Central Political Bureau. During the Central Political Bureau's discussion, everyone agreed with Mao Zedong's idea. Thus, within the central leadership, a unified opinion on establishing the "suspended death sentence" penalty was quickly formed.

1

*   The Establishment of the "Suspended Death Sentence" 

On May 8, 1951, Mao Zedong drafted on behalf of the Central Committee the "Decision of the Central Committee on the Policy That the Majority of Counterrevolutionaries Who Have Committed Capital Crimes Should Be Sentenced to Death with a Two-Year Reprieve." According to the situation at the time, this decision specifically stipulated the proportion of "suspended death sentences" to be imposed. This proportion stipulated that among counterrevolutionaries deserving of execution, only one or two out of ten were to be listed as eligible for the death penalty, while eight or nine out of ten were to be listed as eligible for the "suspended death sentence." Shortly after this central decision was issued, a national public security conference was held in Beijing. This conference established the "suspended death sentence" as a penal term and formed the "Resolution of the Third National Public Security Conference." This resolution was issued after Mao Zedong reviewed and approved it word by word. In his revisions to the "Resolution of the Third National Public Security Conference," Mao Zedong pointed out: "For those with blood debts or other most serious crimes whose execution is necessary to appease public indignation, and those who have caused the most serious harm to state interests, the death penalty must be resolutely imposed and promptly carried out. For those without blood debts, who have not aroused great public indignation, and who, although having caused serious harm to state interests, have not reached the most serious degree, yet whose crimes merit the death penalty, the policy of imposing the death penalty with a two-year reprieve, forced labor, and observing their future conduct should be adopted."

8

On July 1, 1979, the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China was adopted at the Fifth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress of the People's Republic of China and officially came into effect on January 1, 1980. This law stipulated that the applicable subjects for the death penalty were those guilty of "extremely heinous crimes," that the method of execution was by shooting, and it legislatively established the system of death penalty with a two-year reprieve.

Refinement of Legal Basis

*   The 1997 Criminal Law 

On March 14, 1997, the Fifth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress substantially revised the Criminal Law, increasing the number of chapters from 13 to 15 and the number of articles from 192 to 452, thus it became known as the "1997 Criminal Law". Regarding the "death penalty" system, significant changes were made: First, the applicable subjects for the death penalty changed from "heinous criminals" to criminals who commit "extremely serious crimes". This revision marked a shift in the standard for death penalty application from a political slogan-style criterion to a professional legal standard. Second, the clause "death penalty shall be executed by shooting" stipulated in the "1979" Criminal Law was abolished. Given the social conditions at the time, besides "shooting", there were more convenient and economical execution methods such as "lethal injection". Third, the relevant terminology for the "death penalty" was altered. For example, "genuine repentance and reform" was changed to "no intentional crime committed"; "genuine repentance and reform with meritorious service" was changed to "major meritorious service performed"; and "refusing to reform with flagrant circumstances" was changed to "intentional crime committed". A comparison of these changes reveals that the former terms were difficult to grasp, while the latter are easier to apply; the former expressions were less precise, while the latter align better with the principles of criminal punishment. These changes made the system of the death penalty with a two-year reprieve increasingly standardized.

1

*   Criminal Law Amendment (VIII) 

On February 25, 2011, the Nineteenth Session of the Eleventh National People's Congress passed a resolution, implementing the eighth amendment to the "1997 Criminal Law", involving the addition and modification of dozens of articles. Concerning the content of the "suspended death sentence", Article 4 of Criminal Law Amendment (VIII) stipulates that Article 50 of the Criminal Law be amended to: "Where a criminal is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, if he does not intentionally commit a crime during the period of the reprieve, the sentence shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon expiration of the two-year period; if he performs major meritorious service, the sentence shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years upon expiration of the two-year period; if it is verified that he has intentionally committed a crime, the death penalty shall be executed upon verification and approval by the Supreme People's Court (Paragraph 1). For a recidivist sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, or for a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve for intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of dangerous substances, or organized violent crimes, the People's Court may, based on the circumstances of the crime, concurrently decide to restrict the commutation of his sentence (Paragraph 2)." Paragraph 1 extended the timeframe for sentence commutation, specifically changing the commutation for performing major meritorious service upon expiration of the two-year period from "commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 15 years but not more than 20 years" to "commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years". Paragraph 2 introduced the system of "restricted commutation", meaning that for those sentenced to death with a reprieve who are recidivists or have committed the eight specified serious crimes, the People's Court has the authority to decide to restrict their sentence commutation based on the circumstances of the crime. These are the two major new additions to the system of the death penalty with a two-year reprieve made by Criminal Law Amendment (VIII), and they also represent innovations to the system.

*   Criminal Law Amendment (IX) and the Interpretation 

On August 29, 2015, the Criminal Law Amendment (IX) was adopted at the Sixteenth Session of the Standing Committee of the Twelfth National People's Congress. It amended the first paragraph of Article 50 of the Criminal Law to read: "Where a criminal is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, if he commits no intentional crime during the period of the suspended death sentence, his punishment shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon the expiration of the two-year period; if he performs major meritorious service, his punishment shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years upon the expiration of the two-year period; if he commits an intentional crime, and the circumstances are flagrant, the death penalty shall be executed after verification and approval by the Supreme People's Court; if an intentional crime is committed but the death penalty is not executed, the period of the suspended death sentence shall be recalculated and reported to the Supreme People's Court for the record."

4

On October 19, 2015, the 1664th meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court adopted and issued the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Temporal Effect of the Criminal Law Amendment (IX) of the People's Republic of China", which came into effect on November 1, 2015. This Interpretation made relevant provisions concerning the specific application of the Criminal Law before and after the amendment to criminal cases tried on or after November 1, 2015. Article 2 stipulates that for criminals sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve who commit intentional crimes during the period of the suspended death sentence and before October 31, 2015, the provisions of the first paragraph of Article 50 of the amended Criminal Law shall apply. Article 8 stipulates that for acts of embezzlement or bribery committed before October 31, 2015, where the crimes are extremely serious, and sentencing to death with a two-year reprieve under the pre-amendment Criminal Law cannot reflect the principle of proportionality between crime and punishment, while sentencing to death with a two-year reprieve under the amended Criminal Law, coupled with a decision that upon the lawful commutation to life imprisonment after the expiration of the two-year reprieve period, life imprisonment shall be imposed without commutation or parole, may achieve appropriate punishment for the crime, the provisions of the fourth paragraph of Article 383 of the amended Criminal Law shall apply. Where sentencing to death with a two-year reprieve under the pre-amendment Criminal Law is sufficient to achieve appropriate punishment for the crime, the provisions of the fourth paragraph of Article 383 of the amended Criminal Law shall not apply. This Interpretation supplemented the issues concerning the application of the Criminal Law to the death penalty with a two-year reprieve system after the formal implementation of the Criminal Law Amendment (IX).

*   Amendments to the Criminal Procedure Law 

On October 26, 2018, the Sixth Session of the Standing Committee of the Thirteenth National People's Congress decided to amend the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, concerning issues related to the "death penalty" system. Article 250 was renumbered as Article 261, and the second paragraph was amended to read: "If a criminal sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve commits no intentional crime during the period of the suspended death sentence, and upon expiration of the period, commutation should be granted, the executing organ shall submit a written opinion to the higher people's court for a ruling; if the criminal commits an intentional crime, the circumstances are flagrant, and it is verified to be true, the death penalty should be executed, the higher people's court shall submit to the Supreme People's Court for approval; if the death penalty is not executed for an intentional crime, the period of the suspended death sentence shall be recalculated, and this shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for the record."

*   Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law 

On February 4, 2021, the Supreme People's Court held a press conference to issue the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, concerning issues related to the "death penalty" system. This Interpretation clarified that all second-instance cases involving a suspended death sentence must be heard in open court. To further implement the system of second instance as final, improve the trial procedures for death penalty cases, and ensure the quality of death penalty cases, the New Interpretation of the Criminal Procedure Law stipulates that for appeal cases where the defendant is sentenced to death, including cases of death penalty with a two-year reprieve, the second-instance people's court must conduct an open trial; for cases where a defendant sentenced to immediate execution or death penalty with a two-year reprieve does not appeal, but other defendants in the same case do appeal, the second-instance people's court must also conduct an open trial.

*   Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Standardization of the Delivery and Execution of Prisoners Sentenced to Imprisonment 

On December 19, 2024, the Supreme People's Court issued the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Standardization of the Delivery and Execution of Prisoners Sentenced to Imprisonment," which addresses issues related to the "death penalty" system. Article 3 of these Opinions stipulates that for an offender sentenced to death penalty with a two-year reprieve, if the offender is in custody at the time of delivery for execution, the first-instance people's court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling becomes effective, serve the judgment, ruling, copy of the indictment, duplicate of the private prosecution petition, execution notice, and case closure registration form to the detention center. If the offender is not in custody at the time of delivery for execution, for cases investigated by public security organs, the first-instance people's court shall, within ten days after the judgment or ruling becomes effective, serve the judgment, ruling, and the decision for execution of imprisonment to the public security organ that investigated the case; then, within ten days after receiving the notification from the public security organ that the offender has been delivered to the detention center for custody, the court shall serve the relevant legal documents to the detention center. For private prosecution cases and duty crime cases, the first-instance people's court shall serve the aforementioned legal documents to the public security organ at the same level for handling. Article 8 stipulates that after receiving the legal documents for execution delivered by the people's court, the detention center shall, for an offender sentenced to death penalty with a two-year reprieve, deliver the offender to a prison for execution of the sentence within one month.

Applicable Provisions

*   Applicable Subjects 

The death penalty with a two-year reprieve is not an independent type of punishment but rather a method of executing the death penalty. Its applicable subjects are the same as those for immediate execution of the death penalty: they must be offenders who have committed "extremely serious crimes" and deserve the death penalty. There are also limitations on the application of the death penalty with a two-year reprieve. According to Article 49 of the Criminal Law, the death penalty shall not be applied to persons who were under the age of 18 at the time of the crime or to women who are pregnant at the time of trial. The death penalty shall not be applied to persons who have reached the age of 75 at the time of trial, except where death is caused by especially cruel means.

2

*   Applicable Conditions 

According to Article 48 of the Criminal Law, the application of the death penalty with a two-year reprieve must satisfy two conditions. First, the offender must be one who deserves the death penalty; this is the prerequisite for applying a suspended death sentence. Second, immediate execution is not deemed necessary; this is the substantive condition for applying a suspended death sentence and serves as the principle boundary distinguishing immediate execution from a suspended death sentence.

6

*   Applicable Consequences 

The consequences of applying the death penalty with a two-year reprieve involve three aspects. First, if the offender commits no intentional crime during the two-year period, the sentence shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon expiration of the term. Second, if the offender performs major meritorious service during that period, the sentence shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years upon expiration of the two-year term. Third, if the offender commits an intentional crime and the circumstances are flagrant, the death penalty shall be executed after verification and approval by the Supreme People's Court.

6

Calculation of the Period

The period of the suspended death sentence is calculated from the date the judgment becomes final. Any prior detention does not count towards the sentence term. The date the judgment becomes final refers to the date from which the legal document announcing or delivering the judgment or ruling that approves the death penalty with a two-year reprieve is calculated. If the suspended death sentence is commuted to a fixed-term imprisonment, the prison term is calculated from the date the suspension period expires, not from the date of the ruling.

Restrictions on Commutation

On April 28, 2011, in order to correctly apply the provisions regarding the restricted commutation of a suspended death sentence as stipulated in Criminal Law Amendment (VIII) to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Procedure Law and based on trial practices, issued a judicial interpretation concerning several issues in the adjudication procedures for relevant cases. It stipulates that for recidivists sentenced to a suspended death sentence, as well as for criminals sentenced to a suspended death sentence for crimes such as intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of dangerous substances, or organized violent crimes, the people's court may, based on the circumstances of the crime, the personal dangerousness, and other factors, decide to restrict their commutation at the same time as rendering the judgment. If a defendant disagrees with the restricted commutation judgment made by the court of first instance, they may appeal. The defendant's defender and close relatives may also appeal, subject to the defendant's consent.

15

*   Substantive Conditions for Restricted Commutation 

According to the content of the amendment to Article 50 of the Criminal Law by Criminal Law Amendment (VIII), namely the newly added second paragraph concerning the provision on "restricted commutation," it encompasses three substantive situations:

The first is restricted commutation for recidivists. According to the provisions of Article 65 of the Criminal Law, a recidivist generally refers to a criminal who has been sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment or a heavier punishment for an intentional crime and, within five years after completing the sentence or receiving a pardon, intentionally commits another crime for which a sentence of fixed-term imprisonment or a heavier punishment should be imposed. As recidivism reflects a relatively high degree of personal dangerousness, the Criminal Law explicitly stipulates that they shall be given a heavier punishment.

The second is restricted commutation for those sentenced to a suspended death sentence for seven types of serious crimes. Amendment (VIII) stipulates that for any criminal sentenced to a suspended death sentence for crimes of intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, or dissemination of dangerous substances, the court may simultaneously decide to restrict their commutation.

The third is restricted commutation for criminals sentenced to a suspended death sentence for organized violent crimes. "Organized violent crimes" is a new criminal law term created by Criminal Law Amendment (VIII). Theoretically, it is generally believed that organized crimes in the criminological sense can be divided into six types based on their level of organization: simple joint crime, gang crime, group crime, criminal group crime, mafia organization crime, and organized crime with mafia characteristics.

1

*   Basic Principles of Restricted Commutation 

The fundamental principles to be grasped in applying restricted commutation are generally considered by the theoretical community to consist of the following three major principles:

The first is the "principle of legality." This principle is the most important fundamental principle to be followed in criminal judicial work. Paragraph 2 of Article 50 of the Criminal Law stipulates three types of cases for which restricted commutation may be applied to a suspended death sentence. Only when a defendant is sentenced to a suspended death sentence in these specified cases can restricted commutation be considered; in all other circumstances where a defendant is sentenced to a suspended death sentence, restricted commutation is strictly prohibited.

The second is the "principle of proportionality between crime and punishment." Restricted commutation should only be applied to cases where imposing the death penalty with immediate execution would be too severe, but imposing a simple suspended death sentence would be too lenient. The legal wording in Paragraph 2 of Article 50 of the Criminal Law states that for a suspended death sentence, the court "may" simultaneously decide to impose restricted commutation, rather than "shall." This grants judges discretionary space in flexibly applying the law to determine whether restricted commutation is appropriate for offenders sentenced to a suspended death sentence under the "1+8" circumstances (recidivists plus eight types of serious crimes).

The third is the principle conducive to the strict implementation of the death penalty policy. From the perspective of legislative intent, imposing restricted commutation on offenders with a suspended death sentence aims to create conditions for further strict implementation of the death penalty policy. By extending the actual term of imprisonment for some offenders with a suspended death sentence, the severity of the suspended death sentence system can be fully realized. This addresses the previous imbalance in punishment execution characterized by "the death penalty being too heavy and life imprisonment being too light," while also avoiding the misunderstanding that "life imprisonment is being made more severe."

Review and Approval Procedures

Approval Procedure

Article 237 of the Criminal Law stipulates, "Cases where an intermediate people's court sentences a criminal to death with a two-year reprieve shall be submitted to a higher people's court for approval." This provision indicates that the power to approve sentences of death with a two-year reprieve is exercised by the higher people's courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, as well as the Military Court of the Chinese People's Liberation Army.

16

Review Procedure

*   Review of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve 

For a case of first instance where an intermediate people's court imposes a sentence of death with a two-year reprieve, if the defendant does not appeal and the people's procuratorate does not protest, the case shall be submitted to a higher people's court for approval.

16

The submission for review of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve, like that for an immediate execution case, must adhere to the principle of submitting case by case. The materials to be submitted shall include a report requesting review, a comprehensive report on the death penalty with a two-year reprieve case, and 15 copies of the judgment, along with the complete case file and evidence. For joint crime cases, even if only one defendant is sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, the files and evidence of the entire case must be submitted. The content and requirements of the report requesting review, the comprehensive report on the death penalty with a two-year reprieve case, and the litigation files and evidence materials are the same as those for cases requesting review of an immediate death sentence.

16

*   Consequences of the Review 

The higher people's court handles cases submitted for approval of a death sentence with a two-year reprieve differently based on varying circumstances.

1.   For a judgment where the facts are clearly established, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, the law is correctly applied, and the sentence of death with a two-year reprieve is appropriate, the court shall issue a ruling to approve it. 
2.   For a judgment where the facts are not clearly established, or the evidence is not reliable or insufficient, the court shall issue a ruling to revoke it and remand the case to the original people's court for a new trial. 
3.   For judgments where the facts are clearly established and the evidence is reliable and sufficient, but there are errors in the application of law or the sentencing is excessively severe, a ruling shall be used to overturn the original judgment and remand the case to the original people's court for a new trial, or to alter the judgment after reviewing the case themselves. 

Cases remanded by a higher people's court to the original people's court for a new trial shall be tried in accordance with the procedures of first instance. If a defendant is dissatisfied with the judgment or ruling rendered after the retrial, they may appeal, and the People's Procuratorate may lodge a protest.

Significance and value

The death penalty with a two-year reprieve is a unique creation of China in the execution of the death penalty. From the perspective of criminal punishment, it is an innovation unprecedented in both ancient and modern times and a first in both China and abroad. It has been praised by Western countries as the "Eastern death penalty system" and possesses unique historical, social, political, and legal significance.

1

*   Historical Significance 

From a historical perspective, China has a long tradition of emphasizing virtue and being cautious in applying punishment. As early as the Western Zhou Dynasty, the Duke of Zhou proposed the concept of "illustrating virtue and being cautious in punishment." Later, the Confucian school represented by Confucius inherited and developed this idea, forming the penal administration philosophy of "virtue being primary and punishment supplementary, combining rites and law." The "Canon of Shun" from the pre-Qin period contains the text: "For unintentional offenses and those caused by calamity, pardon them; for those who persist in evil to the end, punish them severely." The general meaning is: if a person causes harm to others due to a mistake, it can be pardoned; if they consistently and intentionally commit wrongdoing, they should be severely sanctioned. In ancient China, none was more exemplary in implementing benevolent governance than Emperor Taizong of Tang, Li Shimin. He not only knew how to employ people wisely, encouraged open criticism, and maintained clear-sighted politics but also treated his subjects kindly. He promoted a penal administration philosophy of "using benevolence and kindness to shape human nature, using ritual and righteousness as the guiding principles, fostering transformation as the foundation, and using clear punishment as an aid." He often said to his ministers: "The dead cannot be brought back to life, so the application of law must prioritize leniency and simplicity. Select fair and good people, and those who adjudicate cases appropriately shall be promoted in rank and granted gold; thus, deceit and falsity will cease of their own accord." He also stipulated: "All major punishments (death sentences) must be deliberated jointly by officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery, as well as the Nine Ministers of the Department of State Affairs. Only in this way can unjust imprisonment and excessive punishment be avoided." By the fourth year of the Zhenguan era, only 29 people in the entire country were sentenced to death, inaugurating the most brilliant "Zhenguan Era" in Chinese history. Mao Zedong, who was deeply versed in history, always held the aforementioned historical legal facts in the highest esteem. Thus, "using history as a mirror," he pioneered the "suspended death sentence" system for executing the death penalty, ensuring the implementation of the criminal policy of "killing fewer and being cautious in punishment."

1

*   Social Significance 

From a social perspective, shortly after the founding of the People's Republic of China, it was necessary to mobilize all forces for social construction. In this historical stage, as Mao Zedong said, "We cannot kill too many people; killing too many would lose social sympathy and also labor power." Moreover, according to historical conventions, whenever a new regime was established, it would invariably "grant a general amnesty to the world" to gain popular support. If too many people were killed, it would provide a pretext for reactionary forces both at home and abroad to incite unrest, leading to a loss of public morale.

1

*   Political Significance 

From a political perspective, the establishment of a new regime should demonstrate a new mode of governance. Capital punishment is a highly sensitive political issue and thus must be handled with extreme caution. There was a need to find a solution that allowed for the imposition of the death sentence while also enabling the non-execution of the majority of those sentenced to death. The "suspended death sentence" was the only viable option.

1

*   Legal Significance 

From a legal perspective, shortly after the new regime was established, the state used the "Common Program" in place of a constitution. The rule of law was still being explored, and much judicial work was guided by relevant policies, often making it difficult to grasp precise standards. Faced with the situation at the time, Mao Zedong had the content of his instructions issued as a central decision. Although it was a policy directive, it carried the highest policy authority and had to be resolutely implemented nationwide. This swiftly corrected the tendencies within the "Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries," allowing many death row inmates to be reformed into new individuals through the probationary period of the suspended execution, thereby becoming a needed force for the state.

Legal Basis

*   Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China 

Article 48: [Applicable subjects and approval procedures for the death penalty and suspended death sentence] The death penalty is only applicable to criminals who have committed extremely serious crimes. For criminals who should be sentenced to death, if immediate execution is not deemed necessary, a death sentence with a two-year reprieve may be imposed simultaneously.

Except for death sentences imposed by the Supreme People's Court in accordance with the law, all death sentences shall be submitted to the Supreme People's Court for approval. A death sentence with a reprieve may be imposed or approved by a higher people's court.

Article 50: [Commutation of a suspended death sentence] If a criminal sentenced to death with a reprieve does not intentionally commit a crime during the reprieve period, the sentence shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon the expiration of the two-year period; if there is truly major meritorious performance, the sentence shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of twenty-five years upon the expiration of the two-year period; if an intentional crime is committed and the circumstances are heinous, the death penalty shall be executed after being reported to and approved by the Supreme People's Court; for those who commit an intentional crime but are not executed, the period of the death sentence reprieve shall be recalculated, and the case shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

For recidivists sentenced to death with a reprieve and criminals sentenced to death with a reprieve for intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of hazardous substances, or organized violent crimes, the people's court may, based on the circumstances of the crime and other factors, concurrently decide to restrict commutation of their sentence.

Article 51: [Calculation of the reprieve period and the term of imprisonment after commutation to a fixed-term sentence] The period of a death sentence reprieve is calculated from the date the judgment becomes final. The term of imprisonment after commutation from a death sentence reprieve to a fixed-term sentence is calculated from the date the death sentence reprieve period expires.

6

*   Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China 

Article 261: The death sentence with immediate execution, imposed or approved by the Supreme People's Court, shall be executed upon an order for execution of the death penalty signed by the President of the Supreme People's Court.

For an offender sentenced to death penalty with a two-year reprieve, if, during the period of the suspended death sentence, he does not intentionally commit a crime, and upon the expiration of the suspended death sentence period, his sentence should be commuted, the executing authority shall submit a written opinion to the High People's Court for a ruling. If he intentionally commits a crime, the circumstances are flagrant, and it is verified upon investigation that the death penalty should be executed, the High People's Court shall report to the Supreme People's Court for approval. If the death penalty is not executed for the intentional crime, the period of the suspended death sentence shall be recalculated, and the matter shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

*   Relevant Judicial Interpretations 

According to the "Reply on Whether to Execute the Death Penalty for Theft Offenders Sentenced to Death Penalty with a Two-Year Reprieve Before September 30, 1997, Who Intentionally Commit Crimes During the Suspended Death Sentence Period After October 1, 1997" issued by the Supreme People's Court on September 9, 1998, for theft offenders sentenced to death penalty with a two-year reprieve before September 30, 1997, for whom the death penalty is not applicable according to Article 264 of the Criminal Law, if they intentionally commit another crime during the two-year suspended death sentence period after October 1, 1997, the execution of the death penalty shall not be approved, except where the new crime should be punished by death and immediate execution is necessary. Instead, the penalty to be executed shall be determined according to Article 71 of the Criminal Law, combining the punishments for multiple crimes.

For the trial procedures of cases involving the death penalty with a two-year reprieve and restricted commutation, refer to the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial Procedures for Cases of Death Penalty with a Two-Year Reprieve and Restricted Commutation" issued by the Supreme People's Court on April 25, 2011.

# Death Penalty with a Two-Year Reprieve (Suspended Death Sentence) - China

## Overview
The death penalty with a two-year reprieve, commonly referred to as a "suspended death sentence" (sǐhuǎn), is a unique Chinese penal system where a criminal who deserves the death penalty is sentenced to death but with a two-year suspension of execution. It is not an independent punishment category but a method of executing the death penalty. The system has been praised by Western countries as the "Eastern death penalty system."

## Historical Evolution

### Origin (1951)
- **May 8, 1951**: Chairman Mao Zedong drafted the "Decision of the Central Committee on the Policy That the Majority of Counterrevolutionaries Who Have Committed Capital Crimes Should Be Sentenced to Death with a Two-Year Reprieve," formally introducing the term.
- Mao proposed the idea to separate those who should not be executed from capital offenders, stating: "For those who have no blood debts... the death penalty may be imposed, but with a repulse of one or two years, forcing them to labor and observe their subsequent performance."
- The policy stipulated that among counterrevolutionaries deserving execution, only 1-2 out of 10 were to receive immediate execution, while 8-9 out of 10 were to receive the suspended death sentence.

### Legislative Establishment (1979)
- **July 1, 1979**: The Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China legally established the provision for the death penalty with a two-year reprieve, effective January 1, 1980.

### Refinements
- **1997**: Substantial revisions to the Criminal Law changed the death penalty application standard from "heinous criminals" to "extremely serious crimes" and changed terminology (e.g., "genuine repentance" changed to "no intentional crime committed").
- **2011 (Amendment VIII)**: Extended the commutation period (major meritorious service commutation changed from 15-20 years to 25 years fixed-term imprisonment) and introduced the "restricted commutation" system for recidivists and those convicted of eight specified serious crimes.
- **2015 (Amendment IX)**: Revised Article 50 to add that if during the reprieve period an intentional crime is committed with flagrant circumstances, the death penalty shall be executed; if not executed, the reprieve period is recalculated.
- **2024**: The Supreme People's Court issued opinions standardizing the delivery and execution procedures for prisoners sentenced to suspended death, requiring legal documents to be served within 10 days and prisoners delivered to prison within one month.

## Applicable Provisions

### Applicable Subjects
- Offenders who have committed "extremely serious crimes" deserving the death penalty.
- **Exclusions**: Persons under 18 at the time of the crime, pregnant women at trial, and persons over 75 (except where death is caused by especially cruel means).

### Applicable Conditions (Article 48, Criminal Law)
1. The offender must deserve the death penalty (prerequisite).
2. Immediate execution is not deemed necessary (substantive condition).

### Consequences After Two Years
1. **No intentional crime**: Sentence commuted to life imprisonment.
2. **Major meritorious service**: Sentence commuted to 25 years fixed-term imprisonment.
3. **Intentional crime with flagrant circumstances**: Death penalty executed after Supreme People's Court approval.

## Calculation of Period
The reprieve period is calculated from the date the judgment becomes final. Prior detention does not count towards the sentence term.

## Restrictions on Commutation (Amendment VIII)
The court may restrict commutation for:
1. **Recidivists** sentenced to suspended death.
2. Those sentenced for **seven serious crimes**: intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, dissemination of dangerous substances.
3. Those sentenced for **organized violent crimes**.

### Basic Principles for Restricted Commutation
1. **Principle of legality** - Only applied in specified cases.
2. **Principle of proportionality** - Applied where immediate execution is too severe but simple suspended death is too lenient.
3. **Principle of strict death penalty policy** - Extends actual imprisonment terms to address the imbalance between "death penalty being too heavy and life imprisonment being too light."

## Review and Approval Procedures
- **Approval**: Higher People's Courts (provincial level) have the power to approve suspended death sentences (Article 237, Criminal Law).
- **Review**: Cases submitted by intermediate courts must be reviewed case by case. The higher court may approve, remand for retrial, or alter the judgment.

## Significance
- **Historical**: Reflects China's tradition of "emphasizing virtue and being cautious in punishment" dating back to the Western Zhou Dynasty.
- **Social**: Preserved labor power and public sympathy during the early years of the PRC.
- **Political**: Allowed the new regime to demonstrate a new mode of governance while handling capital punishment cautiously.
- **Legal**: Corrected extreme tendencies in the Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries and allowed death row inmates to be reformed.

**Chapter III Criminal Punishment**

Section 1 Types of Criminal Punishment

Article 32 Criminal punishment is classified into principal punishment and supplementary punishment.

Article 33 The types of principal punishment are as follows:

(1) non-custodial correction;

(2) short-term custody;

(3) fixed-term imprisonment;

(4) life imprisonment; and

(5) death penalty.

Article 34 The types of supplementary punishment are as follows:

(1) fines;

(2) deprivation of political rights; and

(3) confiscation of property.

Supplementary punishment may be imposed independently.

Article 35 Deportation may be imposed independently or additionally on a foreigner who commits a crime.

Article 36 Where a victim suffers economic losses as a result of a criminal act, the offender shall, in addition to being subjected to criminal punishment in accordance with the law, be sentenced to pay compensation for the economic losses according to the situation.

If an offender liable for civil compensation is also sentenced to pay a fine but his property is not sufficient to pay both, or if he is also sentenced to confiscation of property, he shall first bear the liability for civil compensation to the victim.

Article 37 Where the circumstances of a crime are minor and the imposition of a criminal punishment is not necessary, the offender may be exempted from criminal punishment; however, depending on the situation of the case, he may be given a reprimand, be ordered to make a statement of repentance, offer an apology or pay compensation for losses, or be subjected to administrative penalties or sanctions by the competent department.

Article 37a Where an offender is sentenced to criminal punishment for a crime he has committed by taking advantage of his occupation, or for violating the specific obligations required by his occupation, the people's court may, based on the situation with reference to the crime and the need for prevention of repeat offenses, prohibit him from engaging in relevant professions within 3 to 5 years, counting from the date when he finishes serving his sentence or he is released on parole.

Whoever is prohibited from engaging in certain professions but violates the decision made by the people's court according to the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall be punished by the public security organ. If the circumstances are serious, the person shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 313 of this Law.

Where there are prohibitive or restrictive provisions in other laws or administrative regulations governing the offender’s engagement in relevant professions, such provisions shall prevail.

Section 2 Non-Custodial Correction

Article 38 The term of non-custodial correction shall be not less than 3 months but not more than 2 years.

An offender sentenced to non-custodial correction may, according to the situation of the crime, be given an injunction restricting him from engaging in certain activities, entering certain areas or premises, or having contacts with certain persons during the term of non-custodial correction.

The offender sentenced to non-custodial correction shall be subjected to community correction in accordance with the law.

Any offender who violates the injunction prescribed in the second paragraph of this Article shall be punished by the public security organ in accordance with the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Penalties for Administration of Public Security.

Article 39 An offender sentenced to non-custodial correction shall abide by the following rules while serving his term:

(1) abiding by laws and administrative regulations and submitting himself to supervision;

(2) obtaining approval from the executing authority before exercising the rights to freedom of speech, the press, assembly, association, procession and demonstration;

(3) reporting his activities in accordance with the rules of the executing authority;

(4) observing the rules of the executing authority on meeting with visitors; and

(5) reporting to and obtaining approval from the executing authority before any departure from the city or county he lives in and for any change in residence.

An offender sentenced to non-custodial correction shall receive equal pay for equal work.

Article 40 Upon the expiration of the term of the non-custodial correction, the executing authority shall announce the termination of the non-custodial correction to the offender himself and to the entity he belongs to or the community he lives in.

Article 41 The term of non-custodial correction is calculated from the date when the judgment begins to be executed. Where an offender is already held in custody before the execution of the judgment, one day in custody is counted as two days of the term sentenced.

Section 3 Short-Term Custody

Article 42 The term of short-term custody is not less than 1 month but not more than 6 months.

Article 43 The sentence of short-term custody of an offender shall be executed by the public security organ in the vicinity.

During the period of execution, the offender sentenced to short-term custody may go home for 1 to 2 days each month. When engaged in work, he may receive an appropriate pay.

Article 44 The term of short-term custody is calculated from the date when the judgment begins to be executed. Where an offender is held in custody before the execution of the judgment, one day in custody is counted as one day of the term sentenced.

Section 4 Fixed-Term Imprisonment and Life Imprisonment

Article 45 The term of fixed-term imprisonment is not less than 6 months but not more than 15 years, except as provided in Articles 50 and 69 of this Law.

Article 46 An offender sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment or life imprisonment shall serve his sentence in prison or another execution premise; anyone who is able to work shall engage in work for the purpose of education and rehabilitation.

Article 47 The term of fixed-term imprisonment is calculated from the date when the judgment begins to be executed. Where the offender is already held in custody before the execution of the judgment, one day in custody is counted as one day of the term sentenced.

Section 5 Death Penalty

Article 48 Death penalty applies only to an offender who commits extremely serious crimes. Where the immediate execution of death sentence is not deemed necessary, a two-year reprieve may be announced at the same time the death sentence is imposed.

Except for judgments rendered by the Supreme People’s Court in accordance with the law, all death sentences shall be submitted to the Supreme People’s Court for verification and approval. A death sentence with reprieve may be decided upon or be verified and approved by a high people's court.

Article 49 Death penalty shall not be imposed upon a person under the age of 18 at the time of committing the crime or upon a woman who is pregnant at the time of trial.

Death penalty shall not be imposed upon a person aged 75 or above at the time of trial, except where he has caused the death of another person by extremely cruel means.

Article 50 Where an offender sentenced to death with reprieve commits no intentional crime during the reprieve period, his death sentence shall be commuted to life imprisonment upon the expiration of the two-year reprieve. If the offender has carried out major meritorious performance during the reprieve period, the death sentence shall be commuted to fixed-term imprisonment of 25 years upon the expiration of the two-year reprieve. If the offender commits an intentional crime with grave circumstances during the reprieve period, the death penalty shall be executed upon verification and approval by the Supreme People's Court. If, despite an intentional crime committed during the reprieve period, death penalty is not to be executed, the reprieve period shall be calculated anew and the case shall be reported to the Supreme People's Court for the record.

When imposing death with reprieve on a recidivist or an offender of intentional homicide, rape, robbery, kidnapping, arson, explosion, releasing hazardous substances, or organized violent crime, the people’s court may, based on the circumstances of the crime and other factors, concurrently decide to impose restrictions on commutation.

Article 51 The period of reprieve for the death penalty is calculated from the date when the judgment becomes final. The term of fixed-term imprisonment commuted from the death penalty with reprieve is counted from the date when the period of reprieve expires.

Section 6 Fines

Article 52 The amount of a fine shall be determined according to the circumstances of the crime.

Article 53 A fine shall be paid in a lump sum or in installments within the period specified in a judgment. If an offender fails to pay upon the expiration of that period, the fine shall be enforced. If an offender is unable to pay the fine in full, the people’s court shall demand the payment whenever it finds that he holds executable property.

If an offender truly has difficulties in paying the fine due to an irresistible calamity or for other reasons, the payment of the fine may be postponed, or the fine may be reduced as appropriate or be remitted upon a ruling of the people’s court.

Section 7 Deprivation of Political Rights

Article 54 Deprivation of political rights refers to the deprivation of the following rights:

(1) the right to vote and stand for election;

(2) the rights to freedom of speech, press, assembly, association, procession and demonstration;

(3) the right to hold a position in a state organ; and

(4) the right to hold a leading position in a state-owned company, enterprise or public institution, or a people’s organization.

Article 55 The term of deprivation of political rights is not less than 1 year but not more than 5 years, except as otherwise provided in Article 57 of this Law.

Where a sentence of deprivation of political rights is imposed as a supplementary punishment in addition to a sentence of non-custodial correction, the term of deprivation of political rights shall be as long as the term of non-custodial correction and the punishments shall be executed concurrently.

Article 56 An offender who has committed the crime of endangering national security shall be sentenced to deprivation of political rights as a supplementary punishment. An offender who has committed intentional homicide, rape, arson, explosion, poisoning, robbery, or other crimes, which seriously undermines the public order, may be sentenced to deprivation of political rights as a supplementary punishment.

Where deprivation of political rights is independently imposed upon an offender, relevant provisions in the Specific Provisions of this Law shall apply.

Article 57 An offender sentenced to death or life imprisonment shall be deprived of political rights for life.

Where death penalty with reprieve is commuted to fixed-term imprisonment or where life imprisonment is commuted to fixed-term imprisonment, the term of the imposed supplementary punishment of deprivation of political rights shall be modified into not less than 3 years but not more than 10 years.

Article 58 The term of the supplementary punishment of deprivation of political rights is calculated from the date when the execution of imprisonment or short-term custody finishes, or from the date when parole begins. Deprivation of political rights shall, as a matter of course, be in effect during the period in which the principal punishment is being executed.

An offender who is deprived of political rights shall, during the period of execution, abide by laws, administrative regulations, and relevant rules on supervision and administration made by the public security department under the State Council, and submit himself to supervision. He shall not exercise any of the rights specified in Article 54 of this Law during the period of execution.

Section 8 Confiscation of Property

Article 59 Confiscation of property refers to the confiscation of part or all of the property personally owned by an offender. Where confiscation of all the property of an offender is imposed, certain amount of property shall be set aside for basic living of the offender himself and the family members supported by him.

When a sentence of confiscation of property is imposed, the property that the family members of the offender own or are entitled to shall not be confiscated.

Article 60 Where it is necessary to use the confiscated property to repay the legitimate debts incurred by an offender before confiscation of property, these debts shall be paid at the request of the creditors.

# Moving the Mountain: China’s Struggle for Death Penalty Reform

The Li Changkui (李昌奎) case demonstrates the negative effect of public opinion and official interference on death penalty reform in China. The Zhaotong Intermediate People’s Court sentenced Li to death for one count of rape and two counts of murder in July 2010. Li appealed, and the Yunnan High People’s Court revised the sentence in March 2011 to death with two-year reprieve—a uniquely Chinese sentence that is virtually always reduced to either a life or fixed-term sentence.By several accounts, these two trials were not marred by procedural error, and according to a 2008 op-ed by Hu Yunteng, vice-director of the Research Office of the Supreme People’s Court, a suspended death sentence is not out of the ordinary for a homicide case involving personal disputes. (Xinhua reported that Li proposed to one of his victims before the murders but was rejected by her family; the other was the first victim’s little brother.) In the op-ed published by Legal Daily in March 2008, Hu said:
> In the past, when homicide cases arose from contradictions among people and neighborhood disputes, a large number of defendants were sentenced to death with immediate execution; now, however, the death penalty with immediate execution is nearly unknown in such cases.

There was little media attention to Li’s case until about three months after the high court’s verdict. In June 2011, in Xi’an, Shaanxi Province, Yao Jiaxin (药家鑫) was executed for intentionally killing a woman after accidentally hitting her with his car. Media attention to the Yao Jiaxin case started before Yao went to trial in Xi’an and mostly served to decry the heinous nature of his crime. Although Yao was executed in Shaanxi, his high-profile case spurred an onslaught of comparative media reports and forum posts on the perceived leniency that Li had received in Yunnan.

|  |
| --- |
| The brother of Li’s victims holds up a sign protesting Li’s reduced sentence of death with two-year reprieve. Photo credit: Huang Xiuli, Southern Weekly |

Responding to popular appeals for harsher sentencing, the Yunnan High People’s Court held a press conference on July 6, 2011. Judges Zhao Jiansheng and Tian Cheng, the court spokesman, emphasized the need to change the traditional concept of retributive justice. The judges explained that Li was eligible for a lighter sentence because he committed a crime of passion, turned himself in to authorities, and offered to compensate the victims’ family. Judge Zhao asserted that “the Supreme People’s Court requires that the death penalty be extremely carefully applied in cases that are caused by civil disputes and conflicts between married couples, families, and neighbors.”The July press conference indicated that the Yunnan High People’s Court was prepared to withstand public pressure and stick to its verdict of death with two-year reprieve. But the court, citing Articles 204 and 205 of the Criminal Procedure Law, announced a retrial only a week later. Then on August 22 it reversed its decision and put Li back on death row.

The reversal led to demands for retrial from another victim’s family. Sai Rui (赛锐) was 21 when he stabbed a woman to death for refusing his romantic advances. Like Li, he turned himself in to authorities, was sentenced to death by the Zhaotong Intermediate People’s Court, and ultimately sentenced to death with two-year reprieve by the Yunnan High People’s Court. The media did not report heavily on the case before July 2011, and the appeal verdict, issued in November 2009, was upheld.

Timeline of Li, Sai, Yao Cases

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Date | Event |
| 6/18/2008 | Sai Rui murders a young woman at a café in Zhaotong, Yunnan, and flees the scene. |
| 5/2009 | Zhaotong Intermediate People’s Court sentences Sai to death. |
| 11/2009 | Yunnan High People’s Court (YHPC) revises sentence to death with two-year reprieve, citing 1) Sai turned himself in; 2) it was a crime of passion; and 3) first trial sentencing was inappropriate. |
| 5/16/2009 | Li Changkui rapes and murders a young woman and her brother in Zhaotong and flees the scene. |
| 5/20/2009 | Li turns himself in. |
| 7/15/2010 | Zhaotong Intermediate People’s Court sentences Li to death, rejecting the defense’s argument that it was a crime of passion. |
| 10/20/2010 | Yao Jiaxin hits a woman with his car and stabs her to death in Xi’an, Shaanxi. |
| 3/4/2011 | YHPC revises Li’s sentence to death with two-year reprieve. |
| 4/22/2011 | Xi’an Intermediate People’s Court sentences Yao Jiaxin to death. |
| 5/20/2011 | Shaanxi High People’s Court upholds Yao’s sentence on appeal, sends to SPC for review. |
| 6/7/2011 | Yao is executed. |
| 7/6/2011 | YHPC holds a press conference regarding its decision, emphasizing 1) reform of retributive killing; 2) Li turned himself in; 3) lesser social impact of murder cases resulting from personal disputes; and 4) SPC policy of “killing less, killing carefully.” |
| 7/10-13/2011 | YHPC announces trial review procedure, and provincial procuratorate suggests retrial. |
| 8/2011 | Victim’s family calls for a retrial for Sai. |
| 8/22/2011 | YHPC holds retrial in Zhaotong and sentences Li to death, ruling that the trial of second instance was correct in procedure but inappropriate in sentencing. |

Due to its location along the Burmese border, Yunnan deals with a disproportionate amount of drug cases that carry the death penalty. (In 2006 Dui Hua uncovered the only complete timeline giving the number of executions in a Chinese administrative unit, Maguan County in Yunnan. In a county of 400,000 people, six were executed in 1999, the latest year for which statistics are available.) Partly because drug cases are at the intersection of capital punishment and HIV, and partly because of its high number of executions, Yunnan was an early adopter of death penalty reform. In 1997 its provincial capital, Kunming, was the first Chinese city to start using lethal injection. (HIV concerns were pivotal because traditional gunshot executions caused blood spattering that could lead to infection.)

The cases of Li, Yao, and Sai demonstrate that Yunnan continued its commitment to death penalty reform through judicial activism that was not occurring in other provinces. In 2008 the Supreme People’s Court (SPC) approved 92.5 percent of death penalty cases submitted by the Yunnan High People’s Court, three percentage points higher than the national average, according to court President Xu Qianfei. Pressure from vocal retributive-justice supporters did cause the court to explain its actions. But the quickness of the court to reverse its stance and hold a retrial seems more characteristic of orders from above than criticism from below.

In 2007 the SPC regained the sole authority to review capital cases, after which the number of death sentences with immediate execution fell below the number of death sentences with reprieve. According to Regulations Governing Issues in the Review of Death Penalty Cases by the Supreme People’s Court, issued on February 27, 2007, the lower court’s decision to execute should be approved during SPC review if “the determination of facts and application of the law … are deemed to have been correct, the penalty appropriate, and the legal proceedings in accordance with the law” (emphasis added).

“Inappropriate penalty” is the reason both the Yunnan People’s Procuratorate and Yunnan High People’s Court gave for recommending and ultimately conducting a retrial. Both stated that the facts, evidence, and procedures were clear and correct. The language and current judicial hierarchy suggest that intervention may have occurred on the level of the Supreme People’s Court. That said, there is conflicting information on whether death with two-year reprieve falls under the scope of SPC review. In the case of Li Changkui, media reports do not mention that the Yunnan High People’s Court had submitted its initial verdict for review. In an August 22 report on the retrial, however, Xinhua states prominently that the reinstated death sentence is pending SPC approval.

“Abolishing the death penalty … is a good legal ideal that needs to be determined at the national level, it cannot be determined by a court verdict,” Deng Zibin, Deputy Director of the Criminal Law Department of the China Academy of Social Sciences’ Legal Studies Center, told Southern Weekly.

Deng implies that wider-reaching national directives could come on the coattails of this case, but obstacles exist. Writing about the problems faced by SPC review in 2008, the vice-director of the Research Office of the Supreme People’s Court highlighted that 1) “there are strong demands by relevant bodies and personnel to intervene in death penalty review procedures,” and 2) “if there is a rise in extremely violent crime and public calls for more frequent use of the death penalty strengthen, there will be tremendous pressure that will affect whether restriction of the death penalty can be maintained.”

What’s clear is that both the Supreme People’s Court and the Yunnan High People’s Court are advocates for death penalty reform, but that popular opinion and a desire for national uniformity are standing in the way of both transparency and the right to life.

This article analyzes China's death penalty reform efforts through the lens of the Li Changkui (李昌奎) case in Yunnan Province. Li was initially sentenced to death for rape and murder, but the Yunnan High People's Court reduced his sentence to death with two-year reprieve—a sentence that is virtually always commuted. Intense public pressure and media comparisons to the Yao Jiaxin (药家鑫) execution in Shaanxi Province led the court to reverse its decision and reinstate the death penalty.

Key events: Li Changkui committed his crimes on May 16, 2009, turned himself in on May 20, 2009, was sentenced to death by Zhaotong Intermediate Court on July 15, 2010, received a reprieve from Yunnan High Court on March 4, 2011, but was ultimately sentenced to death again on August 22, 2011 after public outcry. The similar Sai Rui (赛锐) case, where a reprieve verdict was upheld, contrasts with Li's reversal.

The article highlights systemic tensions: Yunnan was an early death penalty reformer (first to use lethal injection in 1997), and the Supreme People's Court (SPC) advocates for "killing less, killing carefully." However, public opinion and official interference undermine reform efforts. Hu Yunteng, SPC Research Office vice-director, noted that homicide cases from personal disputes now rarely receive immediate execution. The SPC's 2007 regained authority over capital case review led to more reprieves than executions, but obstacles remain including demands for intervention and public pressure for retribution when violent crime rises.

最高人民法院院长  周强

　　现在，我代表最高人民法院，向大会报告工作，请予审议，并请全国政协各位委员提出意见。

**2021年主要工作**

　　2021年，在以习近平同志为核心的党中央坚强领导下，在全国人大及其常委会有力监督下，最高人民法院坚持以习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想为指导，深入贯彻习近平法治思想，全面贯彻党的十九大和十九届历次全会精神，认真落实十三届全国人大四次会议决议，深入领会“两个确立”的决定性意义，增强“四个意识”、坚定“四个自信”、做到“两个维护”，坚定不移走中国特色社会主义法治道路，紧紧围绕“努力让人民群众在每一个司法案件中感受到公平正义”目标，坚持服务大局、司法为民、公正司法，忠实履行宪法法律赋予的职责，各项工作取得新进展。最高人民法院受理案件33602件，审结28720件，制定司法解释24件，发布指导性案例31个，加强对全国法院审判工作的监督指导；地方各级人民法院和专门人民法院受理案件3351.6万件，审结、执结3010.4万件，结案标的额8.3万亿元。通过发挥审判职能作用，推动建设更高水平的平安中国、法治中国，为实现“十四五”良好开局提供有力司法服务。

**一、坚决维护国家安全和社会稳定**

　　认真贯彻总体国家安全观，依法惩治各类犯罪。各级法院审结一审刑事案件125.6万件，判处罪犯171.5万人。八类主要刑事犯罪案件持续处于低位，占全部刑事案件比重稳步下降，我国是世界上最安全的国家之一。

　　严惩危害国家安全和社会治安犯罪。严惩煽动颠覆国家政权、间谍窃密、邪教等犯罪，坚决维护国家政权安全、制度安全。对资助危害国家安全活动的李亨利依法定罪判刑。审结网络传销、网络赌博、非法利用信息网络等犯罪案件9.2万件，维护互联网安全。严惩危害生物安全犯罪，维护国家生物安全，保障人民生命健康。审结杀人、放火、抢劫等严重暴力犯罪案件4.9万件。会同公安部等出台惩治涉枪涉爆犯罪意见，审结相关案件9984件。审结毒品犯罪案件5.6万件，严厉打击走私、制造毒品等源头性犯罪。审结袭警犯罪案件4586件。严惩暴力伤医犯罪，保障医务人员安全和正常医疗秩序，为医务人员和广大患者创造良好诊疗环境。人民法院准确贯彻死刑政策，对严重危害公共安全、严重影响群众安全感的犯罪，对残害妇女儿童、老年人等挑战法律和伦理底线的犯罪，论罪当判死刑的，依法判处并核准死刑，坚决维护法治权威。

　　依法维护疫情防控秩序。审结涉疫犯罪案件9653件。对故意隐瞒中高风险地区行程、违规接诊发热患者、伪造售卖核酸报告、“带疫偷渡”等犯罪严惩不贷。会同海关总署等发布打击海上跨境走私犯罪意见，严惩走私冻品犯罪，防范疫情传播风险。

　　常态化开展扫黑除恶斗争。健全常态化扫黑除恶机制，防止黑恶势力“死灰复燃”。加快案件清结，审结涉黑涉恶犯罪案件3409件18360人。推进黑财清底，执行到位财产刑及追缴、没收违法所得405.7亿元，坚决摧毁黑恶势力经济基础。推进专项整治，发出相关司法建议3816份。巩固整治“村霸”、“沙霸”、“菜霸”等成果，促进基层社会治理。

　　依法惩治腐败犯罪。审结贪污贿赂、渎职等案件2.3万件2.7万人，秦光荣、王富玉等14名原中管干部受到审判，彰显党中央正风肃纪、反腐惩恶的坚定决心。落实受贿行贿一起查，依法追缴行贿非法获利，斩断“围猎”腐蚀、权钱交易的利益链条。加大职务犯罪赃款赃物追缴力度，实际追缴到位596.6亿元。境外不是法外，首次适用刑事缺席审判程序审理程三昌案，裁定没收外逃人员徐进、张正欣境内外巨额违法所得，对外逃腐败犯罪分子虽远必惩，让其人财两空。

　　维护国家粮食安全。出台服务全面推进乡村振兴意见。会同农业农村部等加强种业知识产权保护，严厉打击制售伪劣种子、破坏种质资源等危害种业安全违法犯罪。审结乱占耕地案件7251件，涉及耕地312万亩，依法惩治农村侵占耕地犯罪，保护耕地红线。辽宁、吉林、黑龙江法院严惩污染、盗采黑土犯罪。

　　维护公民个人信息安全。信息时代，个人信息安全保护变得突出和紧迫。认真贯彻个人信息保护法，严惩窃取倒卖身份证、通讯录、快递单、微信账号、患者信息等各类侵犯公民个人信息犯罪，审结相关案件4098件，同比上升60.2%。依法从严惩治行业“内鬼”泄露个人信息。严惩利用恶意程序、钓鱼欺诈等形式非法获取个人信息，审理“颜值检测”软件窃取个人信息案，惩治网络黑灰产业链犯罪。严惩通过非法侵入监控系统贩卖幼儿园、养老院实时监控数据的犯罪分子。对侵犯个人信息、煽动网络暴力侮辱诽谤的，依法追究刑事责任。出台人脸识别司法解释，制止滥用人脸识别技术行为，让公众不再为自己的“脸面”担忧。审理人脸识别第一案，明确人脸识别技术应用范围，守护公众重要生物识别信息安全。

**三、始终坚持以人民为中心**

　　牢记人民至上，始终把人民群众呼声作为第一信号，及时高效便捷化解矛盾纠纷，依法保障人民群众合法权益，让人民群众切实感受到公平正义就在身边。

　　切实实施民法典。民法典颁布实施，让民事权利保护进入法典时代。适用民法典审理一系列与百姓生活息息相关的“第一案”。审理老旧小区加装电梯案，保障民生工程顺利进行，促进邻里团结和睦。审理好意同乘减轻责任案，鼓励互帮互助，增进社会互信。审理多起居住权案，保障困难群众生活居住需要，驳回“强行啃老”等无理居住权请求。及时签发人格权侵害禁令，为保护生命健康、名誉荣誉、个人隐私等提供预防和救济。民法典实施一年多来，走进千家万户，进入百姓心田，一个个司法案例让民法典条文变得更加鲜活起来，让群众切实感受到民法典就是人民权利的保障书，就是日常生活的法律百科全书。

　　大力弘扬社会主义核心价值观。通过司法断案弘扬真善美、鞭笞假恶丑。审理侵害袁隆平院士名誉荣誉案，坚决维护共和国功勋的尊严。审理女童热心助人致伤案，判决善意助人不担责。审理小区保安送老人就医被索赔案，驳回无理赔偿请求。审理号贩子逃跑摔伤索赔案，判决追赶者无责。审理高铁霸铺案，判决曝光公共场所不文明行为无需担责。对长期霸占已售房屋、耍横抗拒执行的当事人采取强制搬迁措施，决不让“赖而不决”大行其道。通过一系列司法判决，鼓励崇尚英模、邻里相助、助人为乐、志愿服务、舆论监督，决不向耍横霸道者让步，决不迁就纵容恶习陋俗，让广大群众知道法治社会提倡什么、反对什么、禁止什么。

　　促进家庭文明建设。加强家事审判工作，守护家庭幸福的港湾。审结婚姻家庭案件183.1万件。坚决反对家庭暴力，依法严惩施暴者，会同全国妇联推动人身安全保护令落地见效，发出保护令3356份，全面加强妇女儿童权益保护。加强对老年人的司法保护，在判决中落实看望老人的规定。对不赡养九旬母亲的4个儿子依法判令承担赡养责任并予以训诫。通过家事审判，维护和弘扬中华民族重视家庭、尊老爱幼的传统美德。
